verdict.rationale: Gmail's docs confirm support for standard IMAP, POP and SMTP with OAuth 2.0, and its own support page explains connecting third-party clients like Outlook, Apple Mail and Thunderbird with messages and labels synced. That covers the open-protocol access core of the story. However, community reports describe IMAP quirks: IDLE only signals new messages, so read-status changes don't propagate, and developers say Gmail's label model maps awkwardly onto IMAP and needs ID/format-conversion hacks. Those reports show rough edges rather than a contradiction of documented IMAP access, so they limit quality instead of making the verdict disputed. Missing for 10: any JMAP support, a documented user-facing standards-based export (e.g., mbox) beyond the developer-oriented API backup/migration use cases, and IMAP fidelity without the reported sync/label-mapping caveats.
